name: Access to Grade Level Content
title: Access to Grade Level Content
answer: Access to grade level content means giving English learners a way into the same material as their peers, not a watered down substitute. AI can help teachers create texts at different language levels, unit glossaries, and sentence frames so students can learn the content while they build English. It matters because a student who cannot read the science textbook cannot learn the science.

sections.body: The idea is that the first job of AI for English learners is access. A student who cannot read the science textbook cannot learn the science, so the text itself must be made reachable without losing the content. Teachers can use tools such as MagicSchool or Newsela to produce versions of a text at different language levels, keeping the important ideas and vocabulary while making sentence structure simpler. The teacher then checks that the simpler version still teaches the same content. This solves the problem of students being shut out of grade level material because their English is still developing.
sections.heading: The idea

sections.body: In a classroom, a teacher can use MagicSchool or Newsela to create leveled versions of a text for a lesson, then confirm that the simpler version still carries the same content. For vocabulary, a teacher can use AI to draft a unit glossary of key terms with simple definitions, examples, and translations into students' home languages through Microsoft Translator. A bilingual staff member should review those translations because academic terms are often translated poorly. The glossary then becomes a reference students use throughout the unit. For discussion and writing, a teacher can use MagicSchool to generate sentence frames at several proficiency levels, with early level students using simpler frames and more advanced students using frames that push toward academic language.
sections.heading: How it works in school

sections.body: The text reports evidence from two meta analyses. A meta analysis of 42 samples of English learners found that literacy instruction with technology built in had a medium sized effect over instruction without it (Lee, 2020). A meta analysis of studies in China found that comprehensive programs with technology at their core had much larger effects than supplementary activities added on the side, which had almost none (Ni et al., 2022). The text adds that a leveled text is most useful when it sits inside a planned lesson rather than being handed out on its own.
sections.heading: What the evidence says

sections.body: The limits are practical and human. The teacher must check that a simplified text still teaches the same content, so the decision about content equivalence stays with the teacher. A bilingual staff member should review translations of academic terms because those terms are often translated poorly, so the decision about language accuracy stays with a person. A leveled text works best as part of a planned lesson, not as a handout, so the decision about how the text fits instruction stays with the teacher. The text does not say that AI replaces the teacher's judgment or the bilingual reviewer's judgment.
